Subject: Unit economics deep-dive — post-call recap and next steps

Tom / Priya — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on: 

1) High-level volumes: you mentioned 800k–1.2M user-facing LLM requests/month with an average prompt+response token size of ~450 tokens (40% prompts, 60% responses). Please confirm whether that profile is steady-state or includes peak gating.

2) Cost targets: you shared a target operational cost of ~$1,200–1,800 / 1M tokens (net inference cost) at scale and a willingness to accept some model quality trade-offs for aggressive quantization / batching.

3) Business metrics: we discussed converting the technical cost into feature economics — target contribution margin of 40–50% per feature, and CAC payback within 6–9 months for the pilot cohort.

4) Next steps we agreed:
  - You: send a 6-month usage forecast by 11/20 (estimated monthly token volumes and core features mapped to traffic).
  - Us (Aditya + me): we'll produce a unit-econ delta deck (tokens -> $/feature -> margin) and a pricing sensitivity table showing $/1M token at different batching/quantization scenarios; deliver by 11/20 EOD.

Attachments: initial pricing sketch (FintechX_RI_pricing_v1.pdf) and a blank forecast template (usage_forecast_fintechx.xlsx).

If any item above is incorrect or missing, flag and I’ll update. Otherwise — looking forward to your forecast.

Thanks,

Marissa — thanks for the recap, looks right. A couple clarifications before we fill the forecast: 

- The 800k–1.2M is steady-state expectation for Q2 post-launch; our pilot month is ~250k tokens. We include peaks (~2x) during marketing pushes; please show a line for peak cost assumptions.
- Budget range: leadership gave us an initial operating budget of $90k–$120k/month for inference and infra; that’s inclusive of any reserved capacity.
- For feature mapping: our priority is "Smart Replies" (high volume, low latency) and "Contextual Search Summaries" (lower volume, higher token size). We’ll map those in the forecast.

I’ll drop the forecast spreadsheet by EOD 11/20. Appreciate the pricing sensitivity table — can you include a scenario showing minimal-batch (low latency) vs aggressive-batch (cost-optimized) and the expected $/1M token for each?

Tom / Marissa — adding the technical/pricing nuance that will feed the sensitivity table:

- Baseline (low-batch, high-quality): ~ $2,200 / 1M tokens. This assumes per-request latency target < 300ms, no quantization below FP16, and minimal prefix caching.
- Mixed (moderate batching + 8-bit quant): ~ $1,450 / 1M tokens. Latency 350–450ms typical, good quality for customer-facing features.
- Aggressive (large batch + 4-bit quant): ~ $950 / 1M tokens. Latency 500–700ms depending on concurrency; some drop in rare-case quality.

Other levers: prefix caching for repeated context (can reduce effective tokens by ~15–25% for Smart Replies), and model selection — using a slightly smaller architecture for Smart Replies can cut cost another 20% at a small quality delta.

Quick $/feature illustration (using your priority list):
- Smart Replies (avg tokens per action 120, 600k actions/mo): at $1,450/1M -> cost = 600k * 120 / 1,000,000 * $1,450 ≈ $104,400/mo.
- Contextual Search Summaries (avg tokens 1,800, 50k actions/mo): at $1,450/1M -> cost = 50k * 1,800 / 1,000,000 * $1,450 ≈ $130,500/mo.

These numbers show how fast inference cost can scale relative to revenue per feature; we’ll convert to contribution margin given your ARPU / monetization assumptions in the deck.

Attaching the quick sketch (FintechX_RI_pricing_v1.pdf) and the empty forecast for your inputs.

Aditya
